'''William G. McCallum''' (born 1956 in [[Sydney]], Australia)<ref name=brief>{{citation|url=https://math.arizona.edu/~wmc/Biographical/BriefBio.html|title=Brief biography for William G. McCallum|publisher=University of Arizona|access-date=2025-03-02}}</ref> is a retired University Distinguished Professor of Mathematics  at the [[University of Arizona]]. His professional interests include [[arithmetical algebraic geometry]] and [[mathematics education]].

== Education and professional work ==
McCallum received a bachelor's degree from the [[University of New South Wales]] in 1977,<ref name=cv>{{citation|url=https://math.arizona.edu/~wmc/Biographical/mccallumcv.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae|publisher=University of Arizona|access-date=2025-03-02}}</ref> and his Ph.D. in Mathematics from [[Harvard University]] in 1984, under the supervision of [[Barry Mazur]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|22512}}</ref>

He was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] and the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] in Berkeley before joining the [[University of Arizona]] in 1987.<ref name=brief/> He became University Distinguished Professor from 2006 until his retirement in 2018, and headed the Department of Mathematics from 2009 to 2013.<ref name=cv/>

McCallum helped found the Harvard Calculus Consortium with other mathematicians including [[Andrew M. Gleason]] and [[Deborah Hughes Hallett]].<ref name=adps/> He led the development of the [[Common Core]] standards for mathematics from 2009 until the standards were first released in 2010.<ref>{{citation|url=https://fordhaminstitute.org/ohio/commentary/william-mccallums-common-core-testimony-wisconsin|title=William McCallum's Common Core testimony in Wisconsin|publisher=Thomas Fordham Institute|date=November 1, 2013|access-date=2025-03-02}}</ref> In 2014 he founded a company, eventually known as Illustrative Mathematics, to develop teaching resources for the mathematics standards that he helped develop.<ref>{{citation|url=https://news.arizona.edu/news/invention-impact-illustrative-mathematics|title=From Invention to Impact: Illustrative Mathematics|first=Paul|last=Tumarkin|work=University of Arizona News|date=July 24, 2019|access-date=2025-03-02}}</ref>

== Selected honors and awards ==
In 2012, McCallum became a [[Fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |date=25 August 2018 }}, retrieved 2015-01-12</ref>
In the same year he received the inaugural [[Mary P. Dolciani Award]] for distinguished contributions to mathematical education, administered by the [[Mathematical Association of America]],<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.maa.org/the-mary-p-dolciani-award-winner-announced|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321182113/https://www.maa.org/the-mary-p-dolciani-award-winner-announced|archive-date=2023-03-21|url-status=dead|date=August 6, 2012|publisher=Mathematical Association of America|title=The Mary P. Dolciani Award Winner Announced: Inaugural Mary P. Dolciani Award Presented at MAA MathFest 2012}}</ref>
and the [[AMS Distinguished Public Service Award]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]], "for his energetic and effective efforts in promoting improvements to mathematics education"<ref name=adps>{{citation|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201204/rtx120400575p.pdf|title=Award for Distinguished Public Service|doi=10.1090/noti822|date=April 2012|pages=575–576|volume=59|issue=4}}</ref>
